# Langflow PR 13960 transaction fixture

This fixture stores complete source snapshots pinned to merge commit `a69a47ff1b5c99ce9c50edc4df45de4397151f17` (base `b40e4aa02661dcc9d630e1e97a0af45d45e88ae4`). `provenance.json` records each immutable upstream path, complete-file SHA-256, byte range, line range, PR URL, and license. Local source filenames end in `.py.txt`; tests read and parse the bytes as data and never import or execute Langflow code.

The trace-clear route in `source/langflow/api/v1/traces.py.txt` runs a bulk `DELETE` through `session.execute` inside the exact `langflow.services.deps.session_scope` context. That wrapper delegates to `lfx.services.deps.session_scope`. The pinned LFX implementation commits after a normal yield and rolls back an active session on both `HTTPException` and general exceptions. `effects.yaml` records this transaction context contract against the Langflow wrapper symbol. A normal context exit makes commit reachable; an exception makes rollback reachable. Neither establishes that a specific runtime path completed or that data is durable.

The trace-clear handler has no explicit `flush()` or savepoint. The pinned `source/langflow/api/v1/flows.py.txt` snapshot contains a separate bulk-flow path where `db.flush()` occurs after nested iteration and permission checks; it is not attributed to the trace-clear endpoint. The pinned regression test records explicit seed and delete commits. The integration test derives call-site inputs from the pinned trace handler, runs them through the effect-contract auditor and SQL transaction report builder, then runs bounded path analysis over that report. The wrapper contract explicitly declares that this exact context yields its transaction receiver, grounded in both pinned wrapper implementations' `yield session` statements; the path report therefore records conditional normal commit and exceptional rollback reachability for the lexically enclosed stage call. It does not establish which exit occurs, runtime object identity, or durability. The trace-clear handler has no explicit `flush()` or `begin_nested()`; synthetic controls cover flush and savepoint classification.
